proposals: PPAC should publish monthly crude imports by source country and by shipping route — Hormuz, Red Sea, Black Sea and the Cape, so India’s layered exposure, with Russia supplying more than half of crude imports, can be measured rather than pieced together from tender reports.

Public-sector refiners such as MRPL should disclose in their quarterly results the extra freight and insurance cost of cargoes routed to avoid Hormuz and the Red Sea, so the price of the rerouting decisions this piece describes is visible to shareholders and the public.

The Oil Industry Safety Directorate should issue a published standard for drone detection and response at refineries, terminals and tank farms, and report compliance site by site in aggregate, so India’s preparedness is documented rather than absent from the public record.

The Ministry of Civil Aviation should publish the list of refinery, oil-terminal and tank-farm sites it has designated as restricted zones for drone flights, so operators and the public can check which energy installations carry airspace protection.
